questions.question: Using the front and rear brakes at the same time:

options.text: Gives you the strongest stopping power.
Should not be done at highway speeds.
Does not work well for stopping a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you the strongest stopping power.
questions.explanation: The best way to stop in a straight line is to apply both the front and rear brakes fully at the same time. Do not lock either wheel.

questions.question: When making a regular stop on a motorcycle:

options.text: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: For a normal stop, use both brakes at the same time and downshift.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection:

options.text: Should only be done by a professional mechanic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only takes a few minutes.
questions.explanation: Do a pre-ride inspection before every ride. It will only take a few minutes.

questions.question: A helmet is:

options.text: Required only for riders with less than two years of experience.
Required for all motorcycle riders and passengers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required for all motorcycle riders and passengers.
questions.explanation: In Alabama, all motorcycle riders and passengers must wear an approved helmet. Helmets protect your head and neck if you have an accident.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should wear:
questions.correctAnswerText: Full-fingered gloves.
questions.explanation: Wear full-fingered gloves made of strong material. They give you a better grip and protect your hands.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Merge
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that traffic is merging.

questions.question: _________ of collisions between motorcycles and cars are caused by the driver failing to let the motorcycle go first.
questions.correctAnswerText: More than half
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle and car crashes happen because drivers do not let motorcyclists go first. Never assume a driver will let you go, even if they should.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road with flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Stop on the road behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait for the emergency vehicle to start moving.
Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, move to a different lane to give it space. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
You must let oncoming traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red light. You must stop completely and wait for a green arrow before turning.

questions.question: The faster you drink alcohol:

options.text: The faster your body removes it.
The faster it builds up in your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: The faster it builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: When you drink quickly, alcohol builds up in your body. Your body removes about one drink per hour. If you drink more than one drink per hour, alcohol will stay in your system.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, where should your feet be?
questions.correctAnswerText: On the footrests for balance.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests while riding. Do not point your toes downward. Your toes could get caught between the road and the footrests.

questions.question: When the lights on a railroad crossing sign are flashing, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Turn around and find another route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights at a railroad crossing, stop completely. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before you go. Never try to beat a train across the tracks.

questions.question: Where is the greatest risk of conflict between you and other vehicles?
questions.correctAnswerText: At an intersection
questions.explanation: Intersections have the greatest risk of conflict between motorcycles and other vehicles.

questions.question: When entering a turn, when should you change gears?

options.text: Take the motorcycle out of gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you enter a turn. If you must change gears while turning, do it smoothly.

questions.question: What separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction?
questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mean you cannot pass. Dashed white lines mean you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: Under normal riding conditions, how can you best help others see your motorcycle?

options.text: Keep your high beam headlight on.
Paint your motorcycle a dark color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your high beam headlight on.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlight to help others see your motorcycle. Use your high beam both day and night when it is legal and safe to do so.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. What should you wear?

options.text: You do not need brightly-colored clothing during the day.
You should wear brightly-colored clothing during the day.
You should wear dark clothing during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should wear brightly-colored clothing during the day.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Wear brightly-colored clothing when riding, even during the day, to be more noticeable.

questions.question: When riding ________, you face the greatest risk of conflict with other vehicles.
questions.correctAnswerText: Near an intersection
questions.explanation: Intersections have the greatest risk of conflict between motorcycles and other vehicles. Position your motorcycle so other drivers can see you clearly.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what should riders do?

options.text: Keep safe following distances between each other.
Follow each other as closely as possible.
Do not worry about distances between members.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep safe following distances between each other.
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation when riding in a group. This keeps riders close together while maintaining safe following distances.

questions.question: Where is the greatest risk of conflict between you and other vehicles?
questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections
questions.explanation: Intersections have the greatest risk of conflict between motorcycles and other traffic. Watch for cars turning left in front of you.

questions.question: When sitting on a motorcycle, your arms should:

options.text: Have a large bend at the elbow when reaching for the handlebars.
Be slightly bent when holding the handlebars.
Be fully extended when reaching for the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be slightly bent when holding the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handlebars. Bent arms reduce fatigue and let you press on the handlebars without stretching.

questions.question: The oily strip down the center of a lane:

options.text: Should only be traveled on if you are sharing the lane with another vehicle.
Usually provides good traction, unless it is raining.
Should be avoided at all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually provides good traction, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: The center strip is usually oily but provides good traction for riding, unless it is raining. The oily strip is usually about two feet wide. Motorcyclists can ride on either side of it and still stay in the center of the lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the right lane will end.

questions.question: When sitting on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Use your arms to hold up your body.
Sit at an angle so your arms can support your weight.
Sit so your arms can control the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so your arms can control the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Sit in a way that lets your arms control the motorcycle. Your arms should not be holding up your body or supporting your weight.

questions.question: The front brake supplies about how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?
questions.correctAnswerText: About three-quarters
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Which of the following factors may affect blood alcohol content (BAC)?
questions.correctAnswerText: The amount of alcohol consumed
questions.explanation: Three major factors affect a person's BAC: the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast they drank it, and the drinker's body weight.

questions.question: When riding at night, maintain a minimum following distance of:
questions.correctAnswerText: Three seconds.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge distances in the dark. Ride at least three seconds behind other vehicles when traveling at night.

questions.question: Riding directly alongside another vehicle can:

options.text: Place you in the vehicle's blind spot.
Help the other driver see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place you in the vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding alongside another vehicle is dangerous. You may be in the vehicle's blind spot. The driver may not see you and could move into your lane and hit you. Riding alongside another vehicle can also block your escape route.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid danger, you should:

options.text: Use only the front brake while swerving.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Do one action first, then the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action first, then the other.
questions.explanation: If you must brake and swerve, do these actions separately. Never brake while swerving because it can cause your motorcycle to fall over.

questions.question: In the center of a traffic lane, there is usually an oily strip. Motorcyclists should:

options.text: Avoid riding on the oil and grease.
Not worry about the oil and grease.
Find the lane with the least oil and grease.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid riding on the oil and grease.
questions.explanation: Avoid riding on oil and grease. The oily strip is usually about two feet wide. You can stay to the left or right side of it and still be in the center of the lane.
